notes.title: Devlog #23: Week 47 & 48
notes.notes:
[i]Hi everyone! We can't believe it's already Friday! The weeks go by so fast. As always, we have a lot of development to show you. Many interesting things are in the works, and we are getting closer and closer to a new test build.[/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/65431eba69b462d193c4156cac9ae1027940e0d3.gif[/img]
[h2]Changing gaits[/h2]
A preemptive stab at having things done before you need them, we redid the lead change on the newer rig. Even though the lead change will probably not be implemented for a good while, we saw that it would be fast to remake and will eventually be needed. It is also one of the last movement animations that had not been remade from the last rig. With the exception of mirrored animations, which would be what you change between with the lead change.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/ed4e177d7dd0de3029c4d9a878e681d46bc31568.gif[/img]
[h2]Minor adjustments and sharp turns[/h2]
While we usually show an animation that have been focused on for a major part of the week. This week there was a lot of smaller details on numerous animations that needed to be fixed and there was no singular animation that was obviously different from earlier. We did start on some new ones but none of them got far enough that we wanted to share them at that stage. There was one animation that stood out with the most visible changes though; We realized the canter turning animation needed to be more dynamic by leaning more into the direction you are moving. Mostly this was because of the speed and angle the horse turns it looked a little off.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/71e4f217227684065e662a95a4109b802bf73f8d.gif[/img]
[h2]Markings affecting mane color[/h2]
Tobiano patterns and other patterns are fun to make, but lining them up to fit the other parts of the horse deemed to be a little tricky. However, we have found a way to make many variations of mane color splits between white pattern and the horse's original color. We will be testing the system out in the new horse shader, but so far it looks to be working as intended. This way we can line up white patterns with the horse's hairs which will give it a more natural look opposed to just solid hair colors.

Exactly how we thought of and created this solution is currently a trade secret, as we haven't seen this technique done before. So imagine our excitement when thinking of this solution and later finding it to be working!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/d22862e7a2dfced1ba30305ca5eda168a5d7bdb9.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/3f85341c535bdaae08a74023c99edb6ed575ead3.png[/img]
[h2]Color swatches and UI elements[/h2]
Since the end of last week we have been working more on the UI for the upcoming test. Different icons have been made for a few categories such as coat colors, breed, markings and more. For the coat colors we've made an icon/button for each coat that can be chosen for the horse. There will of course be restriction for each breed when more breeds are added to the game. A lot of time has gone into putting the icons and objects together in a program to see how it all goes together. Some icons will change later, but they work for now.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/07bd8ebd58723c170f2e2004306adf62f6fa221e.png[/img]
[h2]Animation data[/h2]
When importing animations into Astride we need to define some additional data like front, side, rotation velocity and when animation events should fire. Good ol' reliable spreadsheets are useful for this purpose. We have a working import pipeline for this now and will keep extending it with extra information. Here’s a screenshot of our fantastic spreadsheet.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/ac4d6c41e0eb0c41581d0548a336c85bd1db0f3d.png[/img]
[h2]Competition arena[/h2]
This competition arena isn’t completely done, but it is at a stage where we are comfortable to test it. There are some things we need to figure out to give you the best experience of this building in the early access. On the curved walls, you see two levels with grass. Our vision is to have some trees and bushes around, maybe even a statue! Who knows how we decide to decorate the arena. But one thing that we know for sure is that we are going to have different banners around the rails! You can read more about it in this public [url=https://www.patreon.com/posts/loyal-supporter-75207716]Patreon post[/url].



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/25737aa865bbd98ea3e889492f9ab045cf5959d7.gif[/img]
[h2]Leg markings[/h2]
We have been steadily adding more and more markings to the horse, and the leg markings finally have their first sets done. All of the leg markings can be changed separately, so in this GIf, you can see the leg markings being randomized. This means that when a player makes a custom horse, they will be able to choose the markings for each leg separately. There will of course be more variations added at a later time, but for now, these leg markings will serve its purpose. 



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/259fa27e1d8459100b275c8de2c534e293d6c088.png[/img]
[h2]Interiors[/h2]
We are also working on some furniture and interiors. We hope they will bring more of a cosy vibe to our game. In the stable, arenas and other buildings, you will find some furniture and other decor elements. Even though the horses are our main priority now, it is good to already figure out how the furniture and other decor will look like. Some of them will have more functions rather than just being visually pleasing. But that is something we will need to come back to on another day. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/2377ff5aaed77b3ffa67d8d99db96bf9fc8027f8.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/0a7deaa8fec59395aa2480611006052be636b7aa.gif[/img]
[h2]Striding progress[/h2]
We’re slowly approaching a testable prototype of the striding system internally. We’ve been working on some visual indicators above the jump to show how in sync you are with the requirements to make the jump. The jump has a fixed speed requirement and a point on the ground where the horse should jump from to make a perfect jump. To show this to the player I decided to add a curved line above the jump to tell you if you should speed up or slow down. A perfect straight line means you have the perfect speed. 

For the striding we decided to have circles showing the frequency and offset you have from the ideal jumping position. If there is a circle on the line it means you have a perfect stride. If it’s not on the line then it’s up to the player to do some mental gymnastics to figure out how much they need to slow down and speed up again to have a perfect stride and still have a perfect speed. It’s a skill players will get to learn over time. The next challenge is having to prepare for the gates after the current one. This will be the metagame in the show jumping gamemode.


[i]Please note that everything shown in these devlogs is mostly just work in progress and is not finished. Changes may happen and the things showcased here will have further work put into them! To see work in progress daily, join our Discord server community [url=https://discord.gg/aucSgbpXXb]here[/url]![/i]

notes.title: Devlog #22: Week 45 & 46
notes.notes:
[i]Hi, everyone! It's that time of the month again and we are back with more work in progress to share with you. It's been an interesting couple of weeks, but we are keeping a steady pace of development for Astride.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/5f26337658a607d4a01275a4bcac47cc9d9e45f6.gif[/img]
[h2]Fast canter[/h2]
During these two weeks we started on adding speed variation animations of the different gaits, as we move move more to transferring and fixing the game engine animation system. We started with the one you see here which was the most needed; the fast canter. The fast canter is as you can surmise, is a faster variant to the canter we already have and will be the fastest animation before being forced into gallop if speeding up. All this is to avoid speeding and slowing down animations to the point of looking silly before they transition to another gait.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/f4da9ca14ff4d83f3b57cf40b2fa449e7080083f.gif[/img]
[h2]Long jump update[/h2]
Continuing from last post the long jump got an update with help from the many suggested references our discord community sent us. We felt that the old animation didn't really sell the jump enough, so the animation got basically redone from scratch since last post.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/34681223b2106255645850358606f0047b6bbc89.gif[/img]
[h2]Striding[/h2]
Striding is an important core feature we need for the show jumping gamemode and jumping in general. It's difficult to show the sheer amount of code that has been written but we promise it's a really cool looking code. We are still in research and development mode, so everything looks broken at the moment in the editor but a work in progress is still just a work in progress. More is to come!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/6792f79cd89aacfa8b78dcaf0ae738fd6430584c.png[/img]
[h2]Horse statue[/h2]
This is one of the statues you can find in Eldheim. The statue is inspired by a few statues we have here in Norway and this fjord is also inspired by an old story from Norway which is called "Vesleblakken" which means tiny, little or small dun horse (Fjord horse). "Blakk" is the Norwegian term for the coat color "dun".  The statue's story will be something to discover in the game.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/78811eb0f9160a6bdf2d3d354cd40279ad41adb6.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/c2b64e250a11c7b31aecd86fce502cbd5481f4f7.png[/img]
[h2]Riding arena[/h2]
Last week we had a little stream session where we made an arena. This will most likely not be the only arena we will have in our game, and even though there were a lot of details we loved about the one we made on the stream, there were a lot of challenges to make it look nice from every angle as well as being functional. So we have held that design for a little bit, and made a more functional one for the early access. [url=https://www.patreon.com/posts/creating-early-74725691]You can read more about the riding arena in this Patreon post[/url].



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/56702ee47508a5faf52b6e77900a27373ff2f678.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/7fd29c3ec6d2c872044bddcce107d0c182860bee.png[/img]
[h2]Tobiano patterns[/h2]
The last couple of weeks, we've been putting work into creating the tobiano patterns and polishing them. Tobiano patterns will be able to come both with and without "mapping" (the borders around the patterns). Polishing these patterns means cleaning up the edges, adding fur for a soft transition, and most importantly - making sure that they align in a good way when adding multiple patterns on top of each other. Since the tobiano patterns for Astride are separated into three parts - the front, the back and the legs - it is important that all of these patterns can work together to create natural looking shapes that would occur in real life. In addition to work on the tobiano patterns, there has been a lot of time spent on social media and community work (you may have seen a small comeback on TikTok). We are currently trying to boost our Patreon with adding more content and rewards for our loyal supporters. 



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/28fa7ef1ad9aa48455f7b35a22cd5fef11a12eb9.png[/img]
[h2]Character concept update[/h2]
For a long time we have used two clothing models for some design ideas for Astride, but these drawings are old and were drawn during the idea phase of the game. And of course as time goes by the art style and art skill has changed a lot for our fantastic artist. We are now aiming towards a semi-realistic look and our artist loved to draw the characters with this art style as well. Stay tuned for some new concepts of clothes that we will show you soon.


[i]Please note that everything shown in these devlogs is mostly just work in progress and is not finished. Changes may happen and the things showcased here will have further work put into them! To see work in progress daily, join our Discord server community [url=https://discord.gg/aucSgbpXXb]here[/url]![/i]

notes.title: Devlog #21: Week 43 & 44
notes.notes:
[i]It's Friday once again and the Astride team has spent the last two weeks crunching away. There has been a lot of work behind the scenes regarding the early access and information on that, as you could probably tell from our earlier update around this. But we do of course have more exciting things to show you this time around.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/2b1e729608e5b3e6323d72ef67cb57db77d0ff62.gif[/img]
[h2]Turning on the forehand[/h2]
Continuing from last time We made it possible to turn the other way around while standing still. EXCITING!
In the GIF you will see that the back hooves have the wrong foot forward. This has since been fixed and you can see the updated version on Instagram, as it should be posted at this very moment.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/a1cf1fd3d3be533d677531370d8baa244542c72d.gif[/img]
[h2]Long jump[/h2]
Another new animation this time! The long jump is; as you guessed, for those obstacles that require fast speeds and long air time. This iteration was mostly made by mixing gallop and the high jump animations with some guidance from references. It is meant to be the framework for the animation it will become, as the solely mixing of those animations does not sell the movement well. We also asked our Discord community if they had or knew of good references that could help lift the animation forwards.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/c07611210ab16aef3be0b422871683e702c6d06c.gif[/img]
[h2]The start of white patterns[/h2]
We have been doing more research around patterns and we just released a new Patreon post with all Mathildes thoughts and progress around horse genetics and colors. Here is the first test of different tobiano patterns where we mix multiple patterns together to create new ones! Since we don't want the standard repeating tobiano patterns that we see too many places. So far it's been working nicely. These patterns aren't polished, so the hard edges will be worked on later.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/c7666e147831a2c8ba83fa39b75886be6c508884.png[/img]
[h2]Striding system[/h2]
The first feature to be properly implemented in early acess is the striding mechanics. This will function as the base on which we will have animations synchronized with the striding frequency and length, and an interesting show jumping mechanic where you have to match the speed and striding frequency the gate expects you to have in order to jump over it.

One challenge is to extract data from real world horse movement and make some sort of a rhythmic movement system independent of visual animations. Luckily we have [url=https://www.horsesandus.com/the-4-basic-horse-gaits-explained]this very detailed blog post[/url] as a reference. 



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/0ac42be360e859298cccc0ee9c01a890bc6f8625.gif[/img]
[h2]Horse controller[/h2]
We are not going to pretend that we are inventing a new horse controller from scratch. Rockstar set the industry standard for horse controllers and just like how Quake set the standard for first person shooter games, we are just going to declare this as the new standard for which quadrupedal movement is done in games. You can learn about how horses behave in RDR2 [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8vtCqfFAjKQ]here[/url].

We’re making our controller behave similar to this one but with our own touch to make it play well with our striding mechanics.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/e45bc1b29e82de57199450fedf435600f8bf9d11.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/3585755b9daa95ac478447a876123bc3551671b0.png[/img]
[h2]Cross country jumps[/h2]
The past two weeks have been mostly spent planning the next six to seven months. However we have been able to make a few 3D models for cross country. Some of you might have seen these jumps already in our Discord server or Instagram. Some of these obstacles will be integrated into the ground, and your horse should be able to jump up and down.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/ffaee2a96ccb01085a3094d54a546625668a00d2.png[/img]
[h2]Jin[/h2]
Meet Rini's husband, Jin! Jin is a 28 year old man and he is the saddler of Eldheim. He is a calm guy who enjoys trail rides in the forest with his horse. He cares highly about his skin routine and enjoys a healthy meal. He got his interest for saddle making at a young age through his family. He was taught by his father and grandfather back in Japan. He got an education as a saddle maker as well which he finished at the age of 20. He spent his early twenties working in Japan as a saddler and that is where he met Rini. 

Rini is a show jumper and was competing on a high level. She was in need for a new saddle for her horse. The two of them fell and love and married a few years later. Jin and Rini wanted to explore the world and spent a lot of time traveling. And that is when they discovered Eldheim for the first time and fell in love with the place. They loved the nature and the people so much that they decided to move there. They built their own house with a small stable fit for their horses and a home area for their rabbits.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/044ddbdd744ade3cdfa0b0bc949efeefcaafd209.png[/img]
[h2]Holiday splash art[/h2]
Since winter is almost here and the holiday season is around the corner, a new splash art is on it's way. There is nothing that screams more "julestemning" than a cold winters day with the sun shining, a fluffy fjord horse and a "julenek" (sheaf) filled with bullfinches that are enjoying a free meal.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/346a525bc2eddb87907187b1fa8762968c972a83.png[/img]
[h2]Pangare and dun[/h2]
We are currently working on the combination of the genes pangaré and dun. Since it's not as simple as adding the pangaré on top of the dun. Pangaré and dun affect each other, so we've made a whole new set of overlays based on these two genes combined. Here is a showcase of all the accepted Fjord horse colors. The Ulsblakk still needs more work and lightening, but the rest are feeling more or less complete. We haven't added the mealy/pangaré naming to the black bases or the double dilutes as they won't show either way. 


[i]Please note that everything shown in these devlogs is mostly just work in progress and is not finished. Changes may happen and the things showcased here will have further work put into them! To see work in progress daily, join our Discord server community [url=https://discord.gg/aucSgbpXXb]here[/url]![/i]

notes.title: Astride early access date and information
notes.notes:
[b]Good morning, everyone. We hope you are doing well! We have some news regarding early access and Astride’s release. While we cannot give exact dates on release still, we have landed on a final countdown towards Astride’s early access (a vertical slice of the full game) release on Steam. For more information about early access, please check out [url=https://discord.gg/7XsMt9jt9V]#ea-information channel the Astride Discord server[/url].[/b]

Last week we had a meeting with the head of the federal funding institution (Norwegian Film Institute) regarding the early access release. In the meeting, we put down all of our cards on the table and asked for an extension of the funding period. With NFI, fundings cover production periods, and with this round of funding, Astride was supposed to end up in early access. The last date of Astride’s funding period was November 28th, which is only a month away and not feasible at this point. But we were granted an extension which will give us up until May 28th to deliver.

[b]What does this mean?[/b] This simply means that we get more time to work on the early access release and make it as polished as possible for us to be comfortable to charge money for.  There have been raised concerns in the community quite a few times now, and we can’t do anything but agree. We would rather push the dates back than release an unstable version of Astride with lacking features. Although our final date is May 28th, we are looking at a release coming in March or April. May 28th is the last day we can deliver our documentation for the period, so we need time to get them in order and sent in.

[b]How does this affect the funding?[/b] Expanding the funding period does not mean we get more funds for the extra months of work we will be putting in. So from November 28th, we have no further funds from NFI to lean on until early access is released and we send in documentation. After this, we can apply for another period of funds from NFI which we will be doing our absolute best to get. Thus, we are reliant on the Patreon funds to keep going the next few months. Thankfully, all of the funds we have gained from Patreon have been put into a savings account which we have kept as a safety net if something were to happen. This will help keep us going and we are eternally grateful for all of the support we have received for developing Astride.

[b]What about a new test version?[/b] We’ve got you! There will be a new version of the Astride test coming before we leave for Christmas and New Years. This version will include the start of a brand new horse controller and a limited horse creator. The horses will no longer have the custom generated solid colors (rest in peace, skittles horses), but we will be testing out the custom horse shader and textures that are currently in the works. You will still be playing as the horse, and you will be able to ride around inside an indoor arena.

If you have any further questions about early access, the release time or anything at all, don’t hesitate to ask questions here or over in the [url=https://discord.gg/7XsMt9jt9V]#q-and-a channel the Astride Discord server[/url]. We will do our best to answer your questions. I would also like to extend a big thank you to our moderators who have been and are so incredibly helpful and kind.

[i]We say it a lot, and we will say it again; Astride wouldn’t have been here without all of you. The engagement, feedback, ideas, support and the most wonderful community we have ever been a part of. Thank you for making this project a reality. We are forever grateful.[/i]

notes.title: Devlog #20: Week 41 & 42
notes.notes:
[i]Hi everyone! It's time for our bi-weekly updates regarding the last weeks work in progress and updates on Astride. There has been a big focus around horse colors, environment and more animations of course.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/6ef16f939d6cc8d1a7863b52d1d54e8896907d05.gif[/img]
[h2]Low jump[/h2]
We redid the low jump using the old as a reference and fixed problems that never got addressed in the old version. But while doing that it never ended up feeling right. Our animator realized he worked himself blind on this animation, so he asked our community to see if they could put words to what was wrong with the movement while adding his suspicions.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/904af553c24541a05e1ab024dc4fc24bbd15e0fb.gif[/img]
[h2]Low jump update[/h2]
Our community was to great help as we got a lot of feedback on what could be the problem, from confirming the animators suspicions to other things that could need a touch up. One of the suggestions added a reference that turned out was in a better angle than the one already used. In the end almost all parts of the animation got scrapped and redone. 

While some problems still persist and will be worked on more, the overall flow of the animation jumped leaps and bounds (badum tss).



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/da86b6413eec701ef0804683360262dac67b7749.gif[/img]
[h2]Turning on the forehand[/h2]
It has been a long time since we added a new animation and not redone an old one. Turning on the forehand is a variant of the old turning of the haunches when the players turn the horse while standing still.

The movement seems easy, but it turned out to be deceptively difficult movement to animate. But after a lot of tweaking back and forth and adjusting tiny joint placements it turned out great (badum tss x2).



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/d955198ec12a7addf32700881c3853556647e9ad.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/ec32cb0333beac3fb9b8cee7ee7b9efde1a5256b.png[/img]
[h2]Points of interest concept[/h2]
For the past few weeks, Maja's tasks has been to draw alot of concepts for many different objects that may appear in the game. This includes different kind of fences, gates, lamps and "points of interest", which means interesting objects the players can discover through out the world of Astride. It can be a special looking tree stump, wood carvings, runes or cairns ("varde" in Norwegian).



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/f2abd68687d385fb9065ae361cf9d5fe6f8c4bef.png[/img]
[h2]Duns, duns and more duns[/h2]
The quest to make more horse color variations is still ongoing, and these last couple of weeks has been mainly focused on that. As the dun gene can affect all horse colors in different ways, there had to be made different shades of dun. For example, the black dun overlay is more grey, while the red dun overlay is brighter and more red in tones to match the underlying color. Dun in single and double diluted creams also needed their own shades. Cremello, perlino and smoky cream dun will be very bright, but still show sign of primal markings if you look close enough. Palomino and buckskin also needed their own shades to match and look natural.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/4702c2cd7e0ff606f346ffe31e8b38c2ddc6cf75.gif[/img]
[h2]Horse coat greying[/h2]
Since all horse coat colors can grey out, we had to scrap the previous greying cycle. The old one was based just on a black horse turning grey, but we needed the greying to work on any color horse. The greying was posted and received feedback of too little pronounced dapples, so this greying will be revised and remade once again to really give the greying process the love it deserves.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/2e1ae499bd810d707a153bfcf6393641d09df1bc.png[/img]
[h2]The new beginning of horse face markings[/h2]
While keeping on the subject of horse colors, markings play a big role in making the horses look more alive and giving them personality. There are a lot of markings that will be added to Astride, but here are 6 of the markings that were worked on during an afternoon. Three of these are Kickstarter markings and three of them are inspired by Patreon supporter horses. We are excited to expand on the horse markings library to make every single horse in Astride unique in their own way.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/8f7e4d3a456bc8cc28c12380ee95a1f3f1c7f5a9.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/3e339473aa6f460f8bb7f7d767f3e0c11b491578.png[/img]
[h2]Maps of Eldheim[/h2]
Some of you might have seen our first draft of Eldheim. We think this version had too much city and too little space to roam with your horse in the nature. Therefore, we have been testing out other maps that will open up more space to explore from horseback. 

We have tested out a faster way to make different types of landscapes. The 3D picture is just a test to see if our pipeline worked out, which it did! We don’t know for sure what Eldheim will look like in the end, but we are positive that with this pipeline and testing, the end result will suit the Astride and have exciting locations to explore.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/08bf3105a89307c017694adc060e67f915a05759.png[/img]
[h2]Player character riding boots[/h2]

notes.title: Devlog #19: Week 39 & 40
notes.notes:
[i]Hi everyone and happy Friday! We've been busy developing Astride these last couple of weeks (as usual) and we do of course have some work in progress to share with you![/i]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/478526770cb710d9da58ea328f9b60bce5ee41e8.gif[/img]
[h2]Tweaking skinning[/h2]
Lately we have been busy remaking animations after updating our rig. This has opened up the opportunity to go over the old animations and make them better. Because of this we have revisited the basic animations first like the walk here, where we lifted the body more as the rig allowed it more than the original. We also got to adjust faults that have been on the back burner for months, like the timing between front and back legs and the back movement. While working so long on one thing it is easy to not be able to see flaws that you are not directly working at, and posting work in progress to our discord got some new eyes to look and notice a skinning flaw that we got to fixing fast.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/160588c28a65d04c11a47289b7d6534b3823d1c9.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/9882eccc64fe3c6ac9265a81b3bc9f9a348122ef.gif[/img]
[h2]Jumping animation[/h2]
As we got to more advanced animations we got a perfect opportunity to show our updating workflow from old movement with deleted leg bones and remaking the animation as much as we could during a stream. You can see we got quite far during our stream, even with some tangents.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/6c751c220fa3a21cdd361c48212014b15cb3e675.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/14bcbace43bc39edafd2e2a456507b2e6d64a3d7.png[/img]
[h2]The start of horse colors[/h2]
As announced on Discord, we have a technical artist working freelance to create a custom horse shader for our horses. We revisited the UV map of the horses and decided it needed an upgrade to work better with the game itself and the shader. This means that we start from scratch with colors again, but it also opens up for creating more detailed layers. There will be an article on our Patreon page in not too long about this. In the GIF above, you can see two chestnut coat variants and the equivalent coat with black and agouti. This means that if Astride has 6 different shades of chestnut/red, there will also be 6 different shades of bay/agouti. There will also be a couple more agouti versions. One with more black and one with less. This will bring the total bay/agouti combinations up to 18 different shades of bays. More and more modifiers and dilutions are being made, such as the mealy/pangare bay shown in the top left collection as well as the buttermilk buckskin in the bottom right corner.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/22399f571fa7f2febdb1eb0495985edcf8458f5d.png[/img]
[h2]Player stable[/h2]
Last time you saw a small piece of the stable textures, and this time the outside textures are done! Our vision was to make something that would make you, as players, feel that you are at an old stable that could need some love and care from you. Whether you choose to maintain the look or do a total renovation is up to you. This stable has 10 stalls available as it stands now. That should be enough for the first phase of the early access. Even though this iteration of the stable is done, it does not mean that the journey is over. Who knows what other stables you will get in the future!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/5f4bb82568400dbfa71711ef9a6f06854111f2a7.png[/img]
[h2]First look at dogs[/h2]
Astride will have some other animals in the game in the future and one of those animals will be dogs. This is a sketch of The Norwegian Elkhound. They are commonly used for hunting and are great companions. And they are quite fluffy!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/a88e9a62e6aaa4d4e5a50b853bf5f6805aee1699.png[/img]
[h2]Player phone[/h2]
There is so much to discover when it comes to the UI, but some plans and sketches has been made. The player will have a phone filled with different apps and here is an idea of how the apps may look like. To ease the player experience and make things more accessible, this is a great solution.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/77ed50c0949b1ddadcc552a984a5de93f8f2d48f.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/b53286f8b51764d8025301c0c66b404d1eba6b1f.png[/img]
[h2]Wavy hair[/h2]
Since introducing the Dole horse to the mix of breeds, we needed to make sure it would get a set of hair to match. Doles are known for growing long, full manes and this is something we wanted represented in Astride. Therefore, we found a way for wavy hair to work. This of course opens up for other horses to have wavy hair as well.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/be7dd1ac6146de40df695b595a52876bc23e2d9b.png[/img]
[h2]NPC house concept[/h2]
Here is an idea for some of the NPC's house. This house is made with Rini and her husband, Jin, in mind. Since they are originally from Japan and moved to Eldheim, they build the house from the ground when they moved there a few years ago. The design is a small mix of a modern japanese house and with some small nordic elements.

The house is light and bright with lots of natural lighting. The rooms are filled with green plants, art and photos. The furniture is in Rini's favorite color aswell as some light wood. Rini and Jin loves to play games together on the TV so they got a console too. In the hallway there some antique objects that Jin bought on an auction which he decorated with some of Rini's showjumping prizes and awards. 

Since Rini have bunnies, the living room have been designed for some space for free roam rabbits with a few beds, feeding space and toys.

notes.title: Early access information and questions!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/0645e2e6df8338acd9d65f9153df9a367521f942.png[/img]
[i]The early access release of Astride is coming soon, and on that occasion, we would like to give you more information about the topic. What early access means for Astride, what to expect and hopefully answers to your questions regarding this. Please take a look at the #ea-faq channel in our [url=https://discord.gg/7XsMt9jt9V]Discord server[/url] if you have any more questions regarding the early access release. If you did not find what you were looking for, don't be afraid to ask questions in the #q-and-a channel over there. You may also leave a comment with any questions in this Steam announcement.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/b3aaec1fd743c547152abdb3e1cfa5c76ed93451.png[/img]
There are a lot of assumptions to what early access is and what it entails. In short, early access is a funding model where the consumers can play a game in various pre-development cycles such as pre-alpha, alpha and beta. Early access is a common approach to obtain funding for indie games. Early access will offer an unfinished version of Astride that is playable, and will be updated and added to over development time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/9bc94f474be7acd36c654e244a3081be27ab4f07.png[/img]
Since Raidho Games is a brand new indie game studio, there are no previous game sales or funding to lean on. To be able to pay our employees what they deserve for their hard work, early access seems like a viable option. That way we can keep working on the project while also generating income for salaries. As an added bonus, we will be able to receive feedback from the players while developing the game, which in return will help us make fixes and changes for a better game experience. Early access is also a great way for players to gain access to the game at a lower price as it will still be in development and not be full price.
While Astride already had a successful Kickstarter campaign, game development is expensive and takes time. The Kickstarter funds helped Astride secure further government funding and traction in the Norwegian game industry. We will keep applying for government funding while Astride is in development, but having the game in early access will help secure the future of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/814824368e87e164f8db9ea9abfe383b075d88ce.png[/img]
From the first early access version of Astride, the game will be very barebones. There will be a working horse controller, jumping mechanism with striding and possibly a dressage move or two. There will be no customization of horses, grooming, feeding, tacking up etc. There will be a limited environment and world to ride in outside. We will be adding a few cross country jumps which will be available in the placeholder outside environment as well as the outside riding arena.
There will be a few horses to choose between from a menu that you will be able to ride. The rider character will not be ready for the first initial version of the early access, but it will come with a later update. This means that in the meanwhile, you will play as the horse without a rider just like the Patreon tests. The player character will need to have its animation synced with the horse and new sets of animations than the placeholder rider from the Kickstarter trailer. The player character is currently being worked on by a character artist and is not done yet. So for now, imagine an invisible rider!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/592ca3ab3303bbbeb15e1a1e92fde46c0f4d6e19.png[/img]
[b]1. When is early access releasing?[/b]
While our statements have been late 2022/early 2023, we want the game to be in a good state before releasing to early access. As of now, it’s looking more like an early 2023 release. While waiting is tedious, we would rather want to release a game with a bit more polish rather than be hasty and deliver a broken state in early access. Game development is unpredictable and issues occur, but we are doing our best to give you Astride in a good state in a timely manner.   

[b]2. Can I play on my Mac/Linux system?[/b]
This is our goal, but will most likely not be available from the start of early access. We will be looking into building the game for Mac first and borrow a Mac to test it for flaws before pushing it on Steam. Building a Mac is not as easy as pushing a button, sadly.    

[b]3. Can I secure early access before it is launched on Steam?[/b]
While the Kickstarter campaign is no longer running, it is still possible to secure early access through our Patreon. However, in November, the early access reward gained from being subscribed 4 months with Bronze or 2 months with Silver will be removed as the early access will be out soon.    

[b]4. What happens with Patreon after early access release?[/b]
The Astride Patreon will still be up and running, but the rewards will have a slight change to them. The early access key rewards will be taken away for obvious reasons, and the other rewards will be tweaked and some might be added.  ‎

[b] 5. What happens with the Patreon testing?[/b]
The Patreon testing will still be available! This means that the Patreon testing will be a more experimental build with more frequent tests and updates, while early access gets updated after. Look at it like this; Patreon testing is the soft launch and test of early access versions before they are released to the public. They might be more buggy and have issues, but will have newer features and test things before being launched to the early access build.    

[b]6. I’m a Patreon, how do I get the early access game key?[/b]
The early access game key will be retrieved in the same way as the testing game key. You will simply have to send a message to @R2-Key2 in the [url=https://discord.gg/7XsMt9jt9V]Discord server[/url] and he will send you your game key. It will be announced when all of the game keys are ready to be redeemed.   

[b]7. Will I need to buy the full game once early access is done?[/b]
As long as you have the early access version of Astride, you will not have to pay for the full version. The early access of Astride will be automatically updated to the full version once it is released. This is why early access is great for consumers as well, as this gives the opportunity to purchase the game much cheaper.   

[b]8. Which languages will Astride be in for early access?[/b]
Astride will only be available in English from early access. Norwegian will be added at a later time. Other languages may be added closer to full release depending on the demand.   

[b]9. How long will Astride be in early access?[/b]
Astride will have its full release once the game has its core gameplay and experience polished and to our standards. As mentioned, game development is unpredictable, so giving an exact date or time is impossible. We have however estimated the full release to happen at around 2025 or 2026.  ‎
[b]
 10. How can I make a change or help with the development of Astride?[/b]
While early access is out, we will have many ways for the community to gather feedback, report bugs, come with ideas and suggestions for further improving the game. Player feedback is incredibly important for us to keep Astride going in the right direction, and any feedback will be appreciated. Once early access is out, we will open up new channels in the [url=https://discord.gg/7XsMt9jt9V]Discord server[/url] and have feedback forms and bug report forms which can be filled out anonymously if preferred.   
[b]
11. What happens with the Discord server after early access release?[/b]
The [url=https://discord.gg/7XsMt9jt9V]Discord server[/url] will have some changes made to better fit the early access and give space for players to find other players to play with, feedback channels, bug report channels and general channels connected to the early access. The work in progress channel will not go down, and we will keep up with the daily posts there. The updates channel will finally start being used to announce updates to builds, patches and changes that are being done. The community part of Astride will stay the same.
 
[i]If you have any more questions or concerns regarding Astride and the early access launch, please don't hesitate to ask. Leave a comment, message us, anything. [/i]

notes.title: Devlog #16: Week 34
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! The Raidho Games team is finally back from their vacation and with that comes more work in progress! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/1290981b82b9bf5a5c5ec46ab0f5d2262021119b.png[/img]
[h2]A new breed in the making[/h2]
As we have finally received all of the breed wishes from the respectful Kickstarter backers, we've started working on the concept art for the breeds. Can you guess which breed of horse this is?



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/dcfaeb6b38ec171f58185073c64153744eca6061.png[/img]
[h2]Stable and stall textures[/h2]
As the first riding arena is ready for Eldheim, the stable and stalls are in focus now. For the early access release we want the players to have a good stable on their property in order to test different features while we develop the game. 



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/1c3827153b8682716e8e5df52db072336f4fd97e.gif[/img]
[h2]Turn at walk[/h2]
Making a horse turn doesn't just require one single animation, but multiple. Turning at a standstill, at a walk, in trot, in canter. It also requires different animations for how sharp the turn initially is. We want to add this amount of detail to the animation to make the horses feel more realistic, as the horses are the main focus of the game.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/2664e7db97ab604c01ca9292c15d4a8d8d1ab8f0.png[/img]
[h2]Map compiler[/h2]
This is the making of a map compiler for our development workflow. The server and client have two different sets of map data. The server has collision. The client has both collision and visuals. A custom compiler is required to split these two into different set of scenes.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/cdf9242d1822f93c8ba176730611ea9d491e4d60.gif[/img]
[h2]Fixing the horse rig[/h2]
The rig has considered being changed for quite a while now, and we finally began the overhaul. It is not finished yet and still has some bugs here and there, but the end goal is to make it easier to work with and avoiding having to tweak the legs for every change made. This will make future animation processes a lot faster. And the best is that the legs no longer defaults to bend at the knee, but uses the pasterns and fetlocks instead - just like real horses do.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/0870164569d8e2eedb571fc3924316adde5401ef.png[/img]
[h2]Another horse breed[/h2]
Yet another horse breed is in the making. This one is definitely heavier! Can you guess the breed?



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/c3969976a6e2e15f6a80fc15c4a16a17e570eca0.png[/img]
[h2]Kickstarter saddle[/h2]
The Kickstarter tack which will be a part of the Kickstarter tack set reward is also in the works. We love some black leather and rose gold metals! And don't forget that feedback on the tack set as we work on it is wonderful so that we can cooperate on making everyone pleased with the result!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/7b3fa40e336c03bb992070f3c6fc998f5988ba5b.png[/img]
[h2]New assets[/h2]
Lastly, a few new assets that will be brought into Astride. Some training cones, a flower pot/vase and a Viking sword cross country jump!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/8e64f69e6c7074ebc7297fcbcfde1dc50ff43b2a.png[/img]
[h2]Horses[/h2]
We are also working on perfecting the horse models for some changes we are making to the rig to make everything work optimal, which will result in a better workflow.  All of the horses are getting some polishing done to their meshes and final touches on their proportions, limbs and faces. There is still a long way to go on all of them, but they're getting better and better!


[i]Please note that everything shown in these devlogs is mostly just work in progress and is not finished. Changes may happen and the things showcased here will have further work put into them! To see work in progress daily, join our Discord server community [url=https://discord.gg/aucSgbpXXb]here[/url]![/i]

Hello everyone and happy Friday! We've had an exciting couple of weeks with more development and game testing.

[previewyoutube=39wNLBkHXX8;full][previewyoutube=39wNLBkHXX8;leftthumb][/previewyoutube][/previewyoutube]

We finally had our first multiplayer stress together with the community to see how far we could push the capacity of the server. The server had a peak at 68 players running around at the same time, which is better than we imagined. There was another stress test yesterday and we will have a third stress test on June 11th, 3pm CEST. Testing is available for all of our [url=https://www.patreon.com/astridegame]Patreon supporters[/url].


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/874d024af855c9ece358d45a9fe84568c1a3b586.gif[/img]

More animations are in progress, and here you can see a very early version of the half pass. It still has a long way to go, but we're getting there!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/d9fdc180d5ec99718b6b20e9119db55c4a27ca3c.png[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/4e99d6a3f5f1e5427d39b18eba742922c169484d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/b3036579f22ac7c1c52fce7dab7237f95d152a4d.png[/img]

More assets for the competition rings are in the works. The judge's booth, scoreboard and podium. There will be a variation of fences and gates around the world. Wood, bricks, plastic, and more. There will of course be more color variations as well.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/f5661decc9fa98d41e46ed1614ffd379be07039d.png[/img]
[h2]Summer splash art[/h2]
We've finally moved on to summer, and that occasion brings forward a new splash art! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/41267d6e69052019aa8dbcbf2aa7384e0c5aee42.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/ae8d4e36f8dbf51f43aa25dbb71dc8b1000ccbaa.png[/img] [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/5114349585f5adeb0e9502115d615709b80deba4.png[/img]

We are still working on the Icelandic horse, but more onto the actual hair and fur. The hair and fur can be used for all of the horses and is why we are spending so much time on it now. What is essentially happening here, is that we are feeding information about which way the hairs should grow. For example, in the hip and flank area, there is a long hair whorl where the fur direction changes three times and merges in different places. This was especially tricky to get right. notes.title: Devlog #9: Week 17 & 18
notes.notes:
Hello everyone! There has been some rapid development these last weeks, and we are excited to show you some of the results!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/bea59370ea4e667120e3e63dea6d48a9891fccbd.png[/img]

We've started to rework the environment with a new tool which will make it much easier to make beautiful, but also natural looking terrain. With this tool, we can generate random nature, but also manual place water, hills and flora/fauna to tailor the environment to fit Astride.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/e7c03b6cb821eef21767daf3e4c0b06ed327566d.png[/img]

We've done some more work on the tack in the works, and it's much easier to make more tack now after we created the tack workshop with all of the different parts to make up the equipment. There will be basic/standard tack, but it is fun to see what we can do with leather carvings and details!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/1574b164013abf586d6a877c6bf6bf83ecd14755.gif[/img]
[h2]Concept for UI[/h2]
The UI is in the early works and here is an idea and concept. This is the first iteration and it will probably change a lot in the future!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/e9d5967559dabf77f60d40eef83aa2a8d90adafb.png[/img]

[h2]Horse controller and multiplayer[/h2]
We've made much progress programming wise. We have a functioning multiplayer through Steam! We've already tested with us five developers in one instance and this worked wonderfully. There is of course still a long way to go, but it's definitely moving in the right direction!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/8da642185154737732bf0f7dd21378448b7b09e1.png[/img]

The Icelandic is sadly taking a bit longer than the other two horses as there is also a lot of other business on the side that has been needing priority. We've also started to explore yet another tool, but this time it's for hair and fur. We are generating our very own hair cards and designing the hair with them. 

Once we get a hang of it, we can make a lot of hairstyles and variations for both horses and humans, but most important; the fur will get an overhaul. We haven't been completely happy with the current fur, so we are scrapping it for something better. With the new tool, we'll be able to create some good looking fur textures, and we are excited to see what the result will end up looking like.

notes.title: Devlog #8: Week 15 & 16
notes.notes:
Hi everyone! We are now in full swing after the Easter break, and we do of course have some more work in progress. It was supposed to be posted on Friday, but was delayed just a little bit due to some travels. This won't be the biggest update as the team has been away (and the last one came back just today), but we do want to share some insight with you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/b5f76a970d4b7ec26addba4c2b3235c1e4cacc35.png[/img]

[h2]Bridles[/h2]
We have been working on updating all of the tack, and here is an English bridle with textures and different variations. The first without a noseband where the hackamore can also be attached, the second one with a regular English noseband and the last with a flash as well. There will of course be color variations, so stay tuned for those!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/3ce78fdcc079c38402e84ab96b3de5698b8c6e15.png[/img]

[h2]Kickstarter Backer badge[/h2]
We were finally able to hand out the Kickstarter Backer roles on Astride's Discord server, and this is what the backer badge looked like in the process. We were able to implement a bot which would add roles to our members for us, which saved a lot of work for both us and the moderators.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/4f7d551e903cbbd7328ec5ae2210968668bfa3ab.png[/img]

[h2]Multiplayer[/h2]
The work on the multiplayer feature has been going strong, and in this snapshot you can see multiple green cubes. These cubes represent individual players and how they interact with each other in a live server instance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/4a91c76c84390a6140d5f2dbb8a5cd6dfe1114df.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/14685998dca3717b27a9cf90898624b96993462c.gif[/img]

[h2]Stopping and turning animations[/h2]
The turning animation has also been in the works! This will be the default turning animation for when the horse is standing and not moving forward. There will be turning on the forehand as well, but this will be added at a later stage. The sliding stop does not mean that we are working on the Western DLC right away, but this animation will be tested as a stage of animation when the horse stops from a high speed, for example from a canter to a halt.

[i]Please note that everything shown in these devlogs is mostly just work in progress and is not finished. Changes may happen and the things showcased here will have further work put into them! To see work in progress daily, join our Discord server community [url=https://discord.gg/aucSgbpXXb]here[/url]![/i]

notes.title: Devlog #7: Week 13 & 14 Progress
notes.notes:
[i]Hi everyone! As you may have noticed, there was no weekly work in progress last week. This is due to a small change. We will be doing biweekly work in progress from now to gather more content for a bigger update to Astride's progress. The Kickstarter campaign has just a few hours left, and the goal is already greatly surpassed. We are so thankful for all of the love and attention Astride has received in the last time![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/13c6b5fb8a4476ca43b3d5a780ed6c9702571e24.gif[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/7d64d3cdbfad1e4661e640fa3ed26cf6b7c67b58.gif[/img]

[h2]Animations[/h2]
We'll start off with animations! These last weeks, we've had a lot of paperwork to be done, as well as other business related tasks that had to be done. But we do have some more animations for you! We've got the horse turning on the haunches for a standard standing still turn. The trot animation has another stage which is a more trained trot. There are still some fixed and work needing to be done, but this is the work in progress this far!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/fcbc499c6d10c16620d7ff9cf7e8817437a76f8a.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/131befa15fb69262b10050882e0a0162b0cf38e7.png[/img]

[h2]Icelandic horse[/h2]
The Icelandic horse has also had more work done. It has gone through the sculpting phase and is ready for texturing. On the left, you can see the Icelandic horse model testing the Norwegian Warmblood horse's textures and normal map. We make sure that all textures work on all of the horse models as this cuts the amount of work needing done for each new horse by a ton. This way, all of the coats and markings can be available for all horses in the future. On the right is the low resolution model already baked and ready for a hand painted normal map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/310b1b0869a320bd2954ffead47433ae18c3b289.png[/img]

[h2]Cross country jumps concept[/h2]
Since Astride also is set in the north with a focus around a Norse inspired theme, we are adding elements to reflect this. Here is a concept of a cross country jump inspired by a viking ship/boat. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/3478184aaa1c6b8c85b2947eb8f1693a86b22c9b.png[/img]

[h2]Bitless bridles[/h2]
There will be many options for tack available in Astride. Bitless is one of them, and here is some work in progress on a hackamore. There will be different kinds of hackamores and bitless bridle options to pick from in the end.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/49972ef1bd5b30dffbc625fd9d10edf93f08d824.gif[/img]

[h2]Engine work[/h2]
There is currently a lot of engine work happening behind the scenes. Here is a test of animations to mare sure that they work as intended and that the speed of the horse and the animation is correct. We are currently working on the multiplayer features, which is why there isn't very much to see at the moment. But this will change soon!

[i]Please note that everything shown in these devlogs is mostly just work in progress and is not finished. Changes may happen and the things showcased here will have further work put into them! To see work in progress daily, join our Discord server community [url=https://discord.gg/aucSgbpXXb]here[/url]![/i]

notes.title: Only 3 days left of the Kickstarter campaign!
notes.notes:
[b][i]Hi everyone! As of today, there are only 3 days left of Astride's Kickstarter![/i][/b]

The Kickstarter has really exceeded all of our expectations, and we are so thankful for all of the support. All of this motivates us so much more to keep pushing and working on the development of Astride and taking the game to its full potential. We would never have been here without all of you.

For those who have been planning on waiting until last minute, this is your heads up! On [b]Sun, April 10 2022 2:16 PM CEST[/b], the Kickstarter is officially done! Keep in mind that the Kickstarter rewards are limited to the Kickstarter only. The tack/equipment set and the signed prints will no longer be available after this. The same goes for all of the other rewards that are currently all gone. You'll be able to pre-order Astride on Steam using Kickstarter. This will guarantee that you have access to the game as soon as it launches for the public.

If you can, we would appreciate any help to spread awareness of the Kickstarter before it's too late. Share it with friends, family or anyone! Anything helps at this point, and we are so grateful to have you all with us. You've given us so much motivation, joy and inspiration to keep going and we are eternally thankful for that.

[url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/astridegame/astride]Support Astride on Kickstarter here![/url]

notes.title: Astride fully backed on Kickstarter!
notes.notes:
We can gladly announce that after only two weeks live on Kickstarter, Astride has reached its funding goal! We are so incredibly thankful for everyone's support in developing Astride. We can't thank you enough!

The Kickstarter however not done yet, we still have 12 more days to go. We do have more stretch goals which will able us to hire another programmer to work alongside Trond to really kick things into gear with development. 

We have to say that we have definitely been overwhelmed with the amount of support that has been shown for Astride, it feels unreal to the entire team. We are incredibly grateful that you all are putting your trust in us to create Astride and make it reach its full potential as a horse game.

Again, thank you so much for supporting us, Astride and being a part of a wonderful and growing community.

[url=https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/astridegame/astride]Click here to support Astride on Kickstarter before it's too late![/url]

notes.title: Devlog #6: Week 12 Progress
notes.notes:
[i]Hello everyone! As usual, it's Friday and we have more work in progress and updates for you. The Kickstarter has been taking off and we are already 94% towards Astride's initial goal! It has really taken the entire team off-guard and we are incredibly grateful to have such a wonderful community with us.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/00f2aa0a2ca0569c8a38c02bc91e5cadbe13951e.gif[/img]

[h2]Animation progress[/h2]
Marius, our fantastic animator, has been working on touching up some of the existing animations. The medium or mid trained trot is one of the animations being worked on and has been improved a lot! This is the seal brown Norwegian Warmblood.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/298b4d2f6d42af12ef6ca1eb5c400590d29ee5d9.gif[/img]

[h2]Horse prediction system[/h2]
Trond has been working more on the prediction feature where he sends the horse into the future to see if it will collide with something, which in return will make the horse react. Above you can see that if the horse is pushed up against the all, its hind end will rotate around the front, creating a turn on the forehand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/1a2f9a47bbe9df741a3c5e9e3450a643b3bc4a25.png[/img]

[h2]Buildings[/h2]
Tirna has been working on some buildings! The riding arena is also starting to take shape. This one will be the more upgraded arena considering its size. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/a1c57331b0cb2a7a1bdc1b4c4715c44a6268c0fa.png[/img]

[h2]Icelandic horse[/h2]
We are also working on a new horse breed, the Icelandic horse! There is still a long way to go with polishing and tweaking, but it's starting to take the shape of an Icelandic. With a fluffy mane and tail it will look even closer to the breed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/d049af6f0b202642aa9bc7140db71984c6337081.png[/img]

[h2]More splash art details[/h2]
Maja has been working on the Easter splash art and we can share some more details! The great tit is a bird species very commonly found in Norway, so of course they had to be included. The art is getting closer and closer to finished, and we can't wait to share it with you.

[i]Please note that everything shown in these devlogs is mostly just work in progress and not finished. Changes may happen and the things showcased will have further work put into them! To see work in progress daily, join our Discord server community [url=https://discord.gg/aucSgbpXXb]here[/url]![/i]

Marius is back to animating and is focusing on adjustments to some animations before starting new ones. Turning animations for canter and trot will of course come soon, so keep an eye open!


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/1ee73dba065e9f174ec9ca7738ed770fb8a0c9d7.png[/img]

Tirna has been putting together the plans for Astride and what we need to focus more on to make Astride be the best it can for the early access. notes.title: Devlog #2: Week 8 Progress
notes.notes:
[i]Hi everyone! Here is our second weekly Steam community update! We've already surpassed 2,500 wishlists here on Steam and we are excited that there are so many interested in Astride. We are currently pushing on the Kickstarter to get it done and ready for launch, but we still have some progress to show![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/2f9767bf954af6407caa819e3ef2a8d44acb9837.gif[/img]

[h2]Horse Rolling Animation[/h2]
Marius has been working on the horse rolling animation here and there, and it's starting to take shape! The rolling animation is very tricky, as this means the entire rig has to be turned around, it's not just the legs moving. It is still a work in progress, and we can't wait to show you guys the finished animation when we get there!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/0fcda1782872a9d838d55d83deec4f34ec48b09f.png[/img]

[h2]Shape Keys[/h2]
To make the horses feel more alive and breathing, shape keys are frequently used for all sorts of things. An example as show here, where the horse is simply enjoying life. Eyes closed and the lip in a "flehmen" as we call it. We want to give the horses personality and quirks. In the middle and to the right, you can see more extreme poses. When the horse opens it's mouth, the bit will follow the jaw and the lips will give way for it. It won't be as extreme in the game, but this way we can make an extreme pose and know that the "in between" will work as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/c7fea2dc15914f914d3644848d0dc32ccd027207.png[/img]

[h2]Splash Art Sneak Peek[/h2]
Easter is [i]almost[/i] right around the corner, and Maja is working on a new splash art for you! Here is a little sneak peek!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/ab44a48e2c4cdd487fa02d353706ccb878061080.png[/img]

Lastly, a postcard from Danceboi, the community given name for this pretty palomino! This is from a scene that will be used as a promotional image, you will probably see it pop up here and there, keep your eyes peeled!

notes.title: Devlog #1: Week 7 Progress
notes.notes:
[i]Hi everyone, here is our first weekly Steam community update! We are happy to finally be able to launch Astride as a “coming soon” game on Steam, and we want to thank you all for wishlisting our game. Astride has reached [b]over 1200 wishlists[/b] already! We are excited to share our progress with you![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/83249b68b815df5ccd98d0b0d9ba29292d764d6a.gif[/img]

[h2]Horse Coat Greying[/h2]
First off for this week’s progress is the fading of horse coats. Showcased here is the dapple grey horse coat aging from a very dark, almost black, into white grey over four stages. This greying process will not only happen to a black coat, but also red, brown and possibly more. We will have to do more research of which coats have a greying process and how we can implement this in the best way possible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/5d0300d99da4f8a8d326e4fd8719369f4aaf1c5e.gif[/img]

[h2]Horse Shaking Animation[/h2]
There has also been a recent update to the horse shaking animation which will come into play after a horse has rolled in the paddock or as a rare idle animation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/d842f805454688a46b534ec564122c1ddc824e24.gif[/img]

[h2]Stable Doors And Systems[/h2]
The stable itself will have many features, and some of the new ones this week are the big outside sliding doors, stall doors and the levels of wood shavings reduce with the amount of shavings that has been used by the player.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41979671/2f20c25a94c45eb77295182dc5cff51fe61a3966.gif[/img]

[h2]Water[/h2]
Moving on to the environment, water has been implemented! The water rises and falls with the waves.
